description: Bean qou-wgnx. Obtains the C1 connection matrix P = Y0^-1 Y_inf and REFUTES the 2026-08-07 degeneracy negative. That negative rested on three wrong premises: (a) the 0-side basis is degenerate — impossible, since p is real so theta_p has real coefficients and the exponents are a conjugate pair, forcing |e_t1(z)| = |e_t2(z)| exactly on the real axis (measured ratio 1.0; scale-invariant conditioning 0.59..0.72, not 1e-18); (b) the bases share no domain — but h entire in 1/z means it converges for every z != 0, so they overlap on 0 < |z| < 1 and match directly with no propagation; (c) |det|/max^2 measures conditioning — it does not, because the Casoratian obeys W(pz) = -(q-1)W(z)/(p^4z^2-1) exactly and so decays analytically while the columns stay independent. Also: P(pz) = P(z) is AUTOMATIC for any two fundamental matrices and was never evidence. RESULT: P = [[c+, c-], [conj c+, conj c-]], elliptic per entry to 1e-27..1e-59; c- has simple poles exactly at z in T p^Z. LIMIT STATED: c+ is NOT an exact constant — its z-variation is precision-independent and grows with q — so 'connection constant' is a q->1 statement, and the asymptotic law is not identified. Stokes multipliers remain OPEN.

verdict: The connection matrix P = Y0^-1 Y_inf IS OBTAINED, and the 2026-08-07 'basis is degenerate' negative is REFUTED on all three of its premises. The 0-side basis was never degenerate: conjugate exponents plus real theta coefficients force |e_t1| = |e_t2| exactly, and the scale-invariant conditioning is 0.59..0.72. The bases overlap on the punctured disc, so no propagation was ever needed. P has exact conjugate structure and is elliptic per entry to 1e-27..1e-59, with c- carrying simple poles precisely on z in T p^Z. NOT CLAIMED: c+ is not an exact constant (its z-variation is real and grows with q), the asymptotic law behind that variation is not identified, and the STOKES MULTIPLIERS ARE STILL NOT EXTRACTED — obtaining the connection matrix is a prerequisite for them, not the same thing. Nothing wired to production.
